verdict.reason: Both debates find the same core split: is the user worn out by the effort, or unsure whether the friend cares? B gets there by reading the user's own words, and its positions narrow visibly under objection, ending in a concrete, observable middle option (a clear handover) that sits between saying nothing and having a talk. A is calibrated and well-behaved, but its exchanges converge more generically, and its key distinction arrives only at the end without anything to act on.

comparisons.a_observation: The Coach objects that a silent test is a trap. The Statistician concedes in A.debate[6].text and moves to wording, and the debate then mostly agrees to 'speak lightly'. The Philosopher's turn in A.debate[5].text largely adds a citation rather than moving the argument.
comparisons.b_observation: The Requester explicitly narrows from 'say something' (B.debate[0].text) to 'handover first, speech second', and gives the cause: the Realist's point in B.debate[8].text that a clear handover is easy to read while stopping is ambiguous. The Generous Friend's request-vs-demand objection in B.debate[7].text is answered rather than restated.
comparisons.why_it_matters: The user's own fallback, stopping texting, is exactly the ambiguous test. B replaces it with a readable one and shows why, so the ending knows more than the opening.

comparisons.a_observation: The effort-vs-being-wanted distinction is raised in the ninth turn and confirmed in the tenth, but A.dependsOn mostly maps it onto 'raise it kindly' versus 'ask a warm question', with similar actions on each branch.
comparisons.b_observation: The Realist ties the reading to the user's phrase 'always the one making plans' as a workload complaint. B.debate[6].text then gives a different sentence for each branch, and B.dependsOn adds a handover trial with a time frame as the step for when the answer is unknown.
comparisons.why_it_matters: The user asked whether to say something. B shows that what to say depends on which worry it is, and offers a low-cost step that produces observable evidence first.

comparisons.a_observation: The three voices are distinct, but several turns open by agreeing with the previous speaker ('I partly agree', 'The Coach has a point', 'Fine', 'Good'), which gives a somewhat uniform, consensual register.
comparisons.b_observation: The Generous Friend challenges both other speakers ('You're both keeping accounts') and holds a dissent to the end in B.debate[10].text, so the stakes differ across the three.
comparisons.why_it_matters: A dissent that survives to the end tells the user that accepting a lopsided friendship is a real option, not a rhetorical one.

verdict.best_of_a: A.debate[4].text: It clearly names why quietly going silent is a poor test: you will read the silence in whatever way hurts most. That directly protects the user from the move they hinted at.
verdict.best_of_b: B.debate[6].text: Two short, non-accusing scripts, one for doubt and one for workload, each tied to a different reading of the user's situation.

concerns.description: Throughout, B refers to the friend as 'she', but the user never gave the friend's gender. It is an invented detail, though it does not change the argument.

It offers a psychological reading of the user's motive (seeking proof they matter). It is explicitly framed as one the user can reject, and B.debate[5].text counters it with an equally plausible reading, so the certainty risk is low.
